title: Design Best Practices Overview
summary: Habits that make a design accurate, buildable, and easy to hand off: complete inputs, clear documentation, and self-QC.

blocks.content: A design is only as good as its inputs. Before laying out devices, confirm you have the spec, drawings, fixture schedule, and any sequence of operation.
Missing a sequence of operation is a common cause of rework — it defines how the controls must behave, not just what devices exist.
When you make an assumption (e.g., substituting an alternative device), record it. The next person to touch the project should understand why choices were made.
A short assumptions/notes list on every design saves hours during QC and commissioning.
Before handing off, verify: device counts match zones, every requirement is addressed, alternatives are noted, and the BOM ties back to the spec.
Treat handoff as if the reviewer has no context — clarity now prevents questions later.

questions.prompt: Why is the sequence of operation important to collect up front?

choices.text: It defines how controls must behave, not just which devices exist
It is only needed for plumbing
It is optional and rarely useful

questions.explanation: The sequence of operation specifies behavior; missing it is a common cause of rework.

questions.prompt: True or False: Assumptions and substitutions should be documented on the design.
questions.explanation: Recording assumptions helps the next person understand decisions and speeds QC.

questions.prompt: What should you verify during self-QC before handoff? (Select all that apply)

choices.text: The BOM ties back to the spec
The office coffee machine is working

questions.explanation: Self-QC confirms zoning/device counts, requirement coverage, and BOM-to-spec traceability.

questions.prompt: What mindset best supports a clean handoff?

choices.text: Assume the reviewer already knows everything
Assume the reviewer has no context and needs clarity

questions.explanation: Designing for a context-free reviewer produces the clearest, most durable documentation.
